status: baseline trained on real licence-cleared data; fails G4, not a deployment candidate
preprocessing: FEATURE_SPEC pad 1.5 -> unpad -> mid-hip/torso normalise -> 15 fps
excluded_reason: fewer than 4 distinct subjects: cannot hold out a subject without leaking identical footage between train and test
scope_limits: Covers only patterns present in licence-cleared recordings; horizontal_pull is absent.
Metrics are within-dataset (PushUpBench subjects), not PhysiqueQuest users.
No claim is made for rep counting; this model classifies movement pattern only.

root_causes: order-invariant global average pooling: a single repeated frame scores 0.4375 vs 0.4688 for the real window
effective test sample is 5 subjects, not 928 windows; per-subject accuracy spans 0.072-1.000
three of seven classes have one or two test identities
representation separates subjects (Fisher 130) better than classes (112)
no facing or camera-roll canonicalisation: mirroring costs 0.142 accuracy
class weights up to 18.8x applied to a class with one training subject

known_issues: trained before subject-id canonicalisation; split code now uses the 8-char prefix and drops one duplicate clip
about 10 of 231 training clips have ambiguous pattern labels (see reports/PATTERN_V1_DATA_AUDIT.md)
all training footage is 1920x1080 landscape 30 fps; portrait phone input is untested
FEATURE_SPEC v1.0 normalises the visibility column, which destroys its 0-1 meaning

quantization.verdict: fails G8: val macro-F1 -0.279, test macro-F1 -0.109, and 10-20x slower than FP32
quantization.recommended_format: static QDQ int8, per-channel, QUInt8 activations, class-balanced calibration
